title: Shape Measures and Typical Growth in the Markoff Tree
content: The positive integer solutions of the Markoff equation are generated by Vieta involutions and form the classical Markoff tree. This paper studies a layer-uniform asymptotic problem which is different from the uniqueness conjecture and from the endpoint Lyapunov spectrum: what is the typical logarithmic shape of a large-level Markoff triple, and what is the typical growth rate of its largest coordinate? For an ordered Markoff triple \((x,y,z)\) with \(x \le y \le z\), set \(u = (\log x)/(\log z)\) and \(v = (\log y)/(\log z)\). We prove the sharp shape-band estimate \[ u + v = 1 - \frac{c(x,y,z)}{\log z}, \qquad \log 2 \le c(x,y,z) \le \log 3. \] Thus every large-level weak shape limit is carried by the line \(u + v = 1\). On this line the one-dimensional layer shape converges, with a quantitative Wasserstein estimate, to the unique invariant measure of the two ordinary Möbius maps \[ a(u) = \frac{u}{1+u}, \qquad b(u) = \frac{1-u}{2-u}. \] Under the change of coordinate \(r = u/(1-u)\), this limiting shape measure is exactly the pushforward of Minkowski's question-mark measure. Hence it is continuous, non-atomic, and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure, and its distribution function is \(q(u/(1-u))\), where \(q\) denotes Minkowski's question-mark function. Finally, we prove an almost sure typical double-exponential growth law. If \(M_n\) is the largest coordinate on a Bernoulli-uniform branch at level \(n\), then \[ \frac{1}{n}\log\log M_n \longrightarrow l_{\mathrm{sh}} \] almost surely, where \[ l_{\mathrm{sh}} = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{1/2} \log((1+u)(2-u)) \, d h_{\mathrm{sh}}(u) = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^1 \log\left(\frac{(1+2r)(2+r)}{(1+r)^2}\right) d h_q(r). \] Numerically, the shape mean is about \(0.32075\), the shape standard deviation is about \(0.09385\), and \(l_{\mathrm{sh}}\) is about \(0.39618\). The source package contains exact enumeration data and code reproducing these constants.
